$comment: Hand-edited (docs/SCHEMA.md). The California Pacific's Napa Valley line and its Vallejo ferry. Research: docs/research/sources-2c/railroads.md, section 3.

lines.name: California Pacific trains, Vallejo to Calistoga

running.note: "Napa Junction to Calistoga 34.48" miles, in the California Pacific's mileage.
"Napa Junc. to Calistoga", in the Southern Pacific's mileage.

lines.summary: Trains from the ferry at South Vallejo by Napa Junction, Napa, Yountville and St. Helena to Calistoga; by 1929, one round trip a day.
lines.fate_note: Discontinued on or about June 1929, with the ferry from Vallejo Junction, in favour of the Southern Pacific's own motor coaches (CRC Decision No. 21194).

sources.note: The Napa Valley Railroad's first train from Soscol to Napa, July 11, 1865; completed to Calistoga in October 1868.
Discontinued under the order of June 10, 1929, effective twenty days from its date: on or about June 1929 (decision 17).

lines.notes: The Napa Valley Railroad ran from steamers at Soscol to Napa from July 11, 1865, and reached Calistoga in October 1868 (Napa County history); the California Pacific, which bought it in 1869, joined it at Napa Junction from Vallejo in 1868-69, at "sundry dates" its own return gives no details of. So when trains first ran from Vallejo to Calistoga isn't sourced: the map draws them from 1880, the first date a source shows the line (decision 20), in the lighter tint. Soscol and the line of 1865 into Napa by Main Street aren't drawn.

lines.name: Vallejo Junction–South Vallejo ferry

running.note: "a ferry line from Vallejo to Vallejo Junction, connecting there with the Northern Railway for San Francisco".
"Ferry—Vallejo Jc. to Vallejo", in the Southern Pacific's mileage.

lines.summary: The ferry across the Carquinez Strait between South Vallejo and the Northern Railway at Vallejo Junction, where passengers changed for Oakland and San Francisco.
lines.fate_note: Discontinued on or about June 1929, with the trains to Calistoga and Suisun, for motor coaches between Crockett and Vallejo (CRC Decision No. 21194).

sources.note: Discontinued under the order of June 10, 1929, effective twenty days from its date: on or about June 1929 (decision 17).

lines.notes: When it began isn't sourced: Vallejo Junction is on the Northern Railway's line of 1878, so the ferry is drawn from 1889, the first date a source shows it (decision 20).
